criteria.no: A required outcome, or its destination, target, mode, or condition, rests on a subjective quality, an undefined label, or an expected output, approval, or standard with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: An outcome is partly concrete, but what to inspect cannot be determined even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.
criteria.yes: Every required outcome, including where it goes and under which condition or mode, is a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, tool use, or identified record that can be inspected.

observable.instructions: Can each outcome that `anchor.statement` requires be checked by inspecting something concrete: a behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool used, or an identified record? Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here. Nothing can be inspected for a subjective quality (robust), a label or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output, approval, or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's say-so with no identified record. A mode the statement defines inline is inspectable. Judge every part the outcome depends on, such as its destination, target, mode, or tier: if any such part is a name the statement never defines, nothing settles compliance, even when the other parts name concrete files or paths.

anchor.statement: When TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set to canary-123 and transport fails, stdout, stderr, and saved run artifacts must omit canary-123 and Authorization: Bearer canary-123.
anchor.quote: test a transport failure with a canary TypeSafe key and make sure console output and saved run files contain neither the key nor its bearer header
anchor.scope: transport-error output and persisted run artifacts
